papers.title: Laser-Induced Solid-State Foaming of HIPed Ti6Al4V-ELI Alloy
papers.abstract: The present work proposes a novel strategy that significantly shortens Solid-State Foaming (SSF) times, delivering a substantial improvement in process efficiency and paving the way for faster production of customized and functionalized prosthetic components. In particular, the evolution of porosity was evaluated in terms of both volume fraction and mean pore diameter and its subsequent effect on microhardness in a Ti6Al4V-ELI alloy that was initially densified via Hot Isostatic Pressing (HIP) and then subjected to Laser-Induced Solid-State Foaming (LISSF). This acronym was introduced by the authors to underline the originality of this approach, which is not reported in the existing literature. Localized heat treatments were performed using a CO₂ laser source at a target temperature of 1020°C, with three distinct dwell times (120, 240, and 360 seconds). To predict density variations and the resulting mechanical properties, two analytical models were implemented and validated: (i) the Johnson–Mehl–Avrami–Kolmogorov (JMAK) kinetic model, which effectively described the time-dependent evolution of porosity and pore growth under different thermal regimes (based on conduction phenomena vs. direct laser exposure) and (ii) the Ryshkewitch-Duckworth (RD) model, which was used to correlate the exponential decay of microhardness with increasing porosity. The experimental results and regression analyses confirm the high predictive accuracy of both models (R 2 greater than 0.95), demonstrating the feasibility of the LISSF process for fabricating titanium components with locally controlled porosity for biomedical applications with reference to the manufacturing of customized and functionalized prosthetic components, ensuring both structural reliability and enhanced performance. On the other side, experimental results demonstrated that process parameters play a critical role in the microstructural evolution: specifically, increasing the dwell time to 360 s under direct laser exposure (1020°C) led to a maximum porosity fraction of approximately 30% and a growth in mean pore diameter up to about 35 µm.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究Ti6Al4V-ELI合金的热等静压后激光诱导固态发泡，但未涉及疲劳性能，与后处理控制疲劳/力学性能的方向相关性较低。
llm.why_not_core: Paper does not evaluate fatigue properties; focuses on porosity and microhardness from a non-standard post-processing (foaming) rather than typical post-processing routes for fatigue improvement.

summary_zh.motivation: 缩短钛合金固态发泡时间以快速制造多孔义肢部件。
summary_zh.method: 对热等静压后的Ti6Al4V-ELI进行激光诱导固态发泡，并采用JMAK和RD模型预测孔隙率与显微硬度。
summary_zh.result: 延长激光照射时间至360秒可获得约30%孔隙率，显微硬度随孔隙率指数下降。
summary_zh.validation: 通过实验与模型对比验证，拟合优度R²>0.95。

summary_en.motivation: To significantly shorten the solid-state foaming process for rapid fabrication of porous titanium prosthetic components.
summary_en.method: Laser-induced solid-state foaming was applied to HIPed Ti6Al4V-ELI at 1020°C with varying dwell times; JMAK and Ryshkewitch-Duckworth models were used to predict porosity evolution and microhardness.
summary_en.result: A maximum porosity of ~30% and mean pore diameter up to 35 µm were achieved at 360 s dwell time, with microhardness decreasing exponentially with porosity.
summary_en.validation: Experimental measurements confirmed high predictive accuracy of both models (R²>0.95).

papers.title: High-fidelity multiphysics modeling of laser powder bed fusion: Coupling laser absorption, vaporization, and powder heat transfer
papers.abstract: Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) involves strongly coupled physical phenomena that are difficult to reproduce and validate. In this work, we develop a high-fidelity multiphysics model within the open-source CFD framework OpenFOAM that overcomes key algorithmic limitations of existing approaches. The model incorporates (i) multi-element vaporization, (ii) temperature- and phase-dependent laser absorptivity, (iii) a computationally efficient treatment of laser attenuation and scattering by the vapor plume, and (iv) an improved powder-bed representation using a non-binary initialization of the Volume of Fluid (VOF) field. This approach avoids artificial interface diffusion and enables accurate prediction of powder–gas free surfaces, thermal conductivity in partially dense regions, laser reflections, and melt pool heat transfer. The model is validated against in-situ synchrotron X-ray imaging and laser absorption measurements for Ti-6Al-4V and SS316L over a wide processing window. The results show that neglecting any of these physical contributions leads to substantial errors in melt pool morphology and absorbed energy. A sensitivity analysis quantifies the influence of individual material and process parameters. Overall, the model bridges critical gaps between simulation and in-situ characterization and provides a predictive and extensible framework for advancing LPBF process understanding. • A high-fidelity multiphysics LPBF model is developed in OpenFOAM. • Realistic powder-bed heat transfer is captured using non-binary VOF initialization. • Temperature- and phase-dependent laser absorptivity and vapor plume attenuation are included. • The model is validated against in-situ synchrotron imaging and laser absorption data. • Sensitivity analysis quantifies the influence of key physical mechanisms on melt pool behavior.

llm.why_not_core: This paper models LPBF process physics (laser absorption, vaporization, melt pool) and does not report any mechanical properties or fatigue behavior of Ti-6Al-4V.

summary_zh.method: 在OpenFOAM中开发高保真多物理场模型，考虑多元素汽化、温度/相依赖性吸收率、蒸汽羽流衰减及改进粉床表示。
summary_zh.result: 模型可准确预测熔池形态和吸收能量，忽略任何物理贡献将导致显著误差。
summary_zh.validation: 基于原位同步辐射X射线成像和激光吸收测量进行验证。

summary_en.motivation: Accurate multiphysics modeling of LPBF is challenging due to strongly coupled phenomena and algorithmic limitations of existing approaches.
summary_en.method: A high-fidelity multiphysics model is developed in OpenFOAM incorporating multi-element vaporization, temperature- and phase-dependent laser absorptivity, vapor plume attenuation, and a non-binary VOF powder bed initialization.
summary_en.result: The model accurately predicts melt pool morphology and absorbed energy, showing that neglecting any physics leads to substantial errors.
summary_en.validation: Validated against in-situ synchrotron X-ray imaging and laser absorption measurements for Ti-6Al-4V and SS316L.

papers.title: Environmental Impact Assessment of Ti6Al4V Chips Recycling Using Shear Assisted Processing and Extrusion (ShAPE)
papers.abstract: Titanium alloys combine strength, low weight, and corrosion resistance, making them vital in high-performance industries; yet machining generates substantial chips that is difficult to recycle via conventional remelting due to contamination and high energy requirements, reducing material sustainability. Solid-state recycling methods, like Shear Assisted Processing and Extrusion (ShAPE), provide a promising alternative by consolidating chips below the melting point while preserving alloy chemistry. This study assesses the environmental performance of ShAPE across a system boundary spanning degreasing through consolidation and extrusion. Impacts were quantified using Cumulative Energy Demand (CED), Global Warming Potential, Environmental Footprint, Average Dissipation Rate (ADR), and Lost Potential Value (LPV), with ADR and LPV applied for the first time to solid-state recycling of scrap from discrete manufacturing. Scenario analyses addressed variations in torque, argon consumption, and electricity mix. Energy demand and CO 2 -eq for the ShAPE process were estimated at 279.51-567.75 MJ and 17.22-32.35 kg per kg of wire, respectively, with sensitivity analysis showing that variations in torque constitute the dominant determinant of these environmental outcomes. While energy demand is comparable to, or moderately lower than, that of traditional wire fabrication only under low-and baseline-torque conditions, ShAPE substantially reduces the resource dissipation and lost material values, with its overall environmental impacts further decreasing by 45.45% when powered with greener electricity. These results highlight ShAPE as a viable route for circular titanium production, preserving material value & reducing dependence on primary extraction.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究钛合金切屑的固态回收，与增材制造Ti-6Al-4V的后处理及疲劳性能无关。
llm.why_not_core: Paper studies recycling of machining chips, not post-processing of additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V; no mechanical performance data, no fatigue or tensile results, no connection to AM.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估固态回收钛合金切屑的环境影响，替代高能耗重熔法
summary_zh.method: 使用剪切辅助加工与挤压(ShAPE)进行切屑固结，并计算全生命周期环境影响
summary_zh.result: ShAPE能耗与传统方法相当但显著降低资源耗散，绿色电力可减少45%环境影响
summary_zh.validation: 基于累积能量需求、全球变暖潜能等指标的场景分析

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate the environmental performance of solid-state recycling of Ti6Al4V chips as an alternative to energy-intensive remelting.
summary_en.method: Life cycle assessment of Shear Assisted Processing and Extrusion (ShAPE) including degreasing, consolidation, and extrusion, with scenario analysis of torque, argon consumption, and electricity mix.
summary_en.result: ShAPE shows energy demand comparable to conventional wire fabrication under low torque but significantly reduces resource dissipation and lost material value; green electricity cuts impacts by 45%.
summary_en.validation: Environmental indicators (CED, GWP, ADR, LPV) calculated using literature data and sensitivity analysis.
